definition: Annual fee deducted from mutual fund assets to pay distribution and marketing costs. Max 0.25% for a fund that calls itself no-load.
Unsecured corporate bond backed only by the issuer's full faith and credit.
A bond quoted by its yield to maturity. Yield above coupon means discount; yield below coupon means premium.
Long-term right to buy stock at a fixed price, usually above the market price at issuance. Often attached to bonds as a sweetener.
Direct participation program. Flow-through entity (usually a limited partnership); income and losses pass to investors. Losses are passive.
Same day as the record date under T+1 settlement. Buyers on or after the ex-date do not get the dividend.
